title: Merge two lists, alternating
description: Write a function `interleave(a, b)` that returns a new list alternating elements from `a` and `b`, starting with `a`. Assume both lists have the same length.
hints: You're walking through both lists at the same position at the same time, so you'll need the index, not just the values.
Loop using `enumerate(a)` (or `range(len(a))`), and for each index append both `a[index]` and `b[index]`.

result = []
for index, value in enumerate(a):
    result.append(value)
    result.append(b[index])
return result
expected_behavior: Returns a list twice the length of the inputs, alternating a/b.
explanation: `enumerate(a)` gives us the index we need to reach into `b` at the same position, so each loop iteration appends one element from each list, in a-then-b order.
